name: tabs
purpose: WAI-ARIA APG Tabs: a labelled tablist of native buttons with a roving tabindex and one tabpanel per tab, automatic or manual activation, horizontal or vertical orientation, RTL-aware arrow keys, and a scrolling tablist on overflow.
whenToUse: Switching between peer views of related content in the same context, such as Overview, Activity, and Settings.
Reducing page length when users need only one section at a time.
whenNotToUse: Sequential steps: use a stepper or wizard.
Navigating between pages or routes: use links (navigation bar, breadcrumb).
Content users need to compare side by side.
Many sections users read in order: use headings or an accordion.
responsive: The horizontal tablist never wraps: it scrolls horizontally (thin scrollbar) and the selected tab is scrolled into view without scrolling the page. Tabs keep a minimum touch-target height. Vertical tabs sit at the inline start of the panels.
rtl: Logical properties throughout. Left/Right arrow keys are mirrored when direction is rtl (configured, or inherited from an ancestor dir attribute). The vertical indicator sits on the inline-start edge.
theme: Selected tab: color-primary indicator on the block-end (horizontal) or inline-start (vertical) edge plus semibold weight, so selection is not conveyed by color alone. Hover uses color-hover; focus uses the shared focus ring. Forced-colors mode draws the indicator in Highlight.
security: Tab labels and string panel content are rendered with textContent, never parsed as HTML. Node content is inserted as provided (the consumer owns it). CSP-safe.
dataHandling: No persistence, network access, or telemetry.

performance.testedScale: 20 tabs in an overflowing tablist in the unit tests.

limitations: Panels are always in the DOM (hidden when inactive); lazy content is the consumer's responsibility, for example on aui-change.
Tabs cannot be closed, reordered, or added by the user.
No scroll buttons for an overflowing tablist; it scrolls natively (wheel, touch, keyboard focus).
unsupported: Rendering HTML strings as labels or content (pass a Node instead).
Tabs as links to separate URLs (use a navigation component).
antiPatterns: Hiding content users must compare in different tabs.
